description: SpaceXplore Tchiowa is an Angola-based team, joining NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We explore NASA Earth observation data can support farmers conditions and crop rotation decisions. We welcome participants interested in agriculture, Earth science, data, AI/ML, software, geospatial technology, climate, design, and storytelling. We value collaboration, creativity, and scientific responsibility.
summary:
SpaceXplore Tchiowa is a digital agricultural platform designed to help farmers organize their farms, manage field plots, monitor crop cycles, and better understand environmental conditions using NASA Earth observation data.
Developed in response to the “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data” challenge, the platform allows users to register farms, define their geographical boundaries, divide them into plots, record crop information, and maintain agricultural activity histories. It also integrates NASA POWER data to provide environmental and climate-related information that can support more informed agricultural planning.
By combining farmer-provided field information with open NASA data, SpaceXplore Tchiowa aims to improve farm organization, agricultural monitoring, and resilience to changing environmental conditions, particularly for small-scale and developing agricultural communities.
details: Project Description 1. THE PROBLEM Agricultural management requires farmers to understand their land, organize crop production, and respond to changing environmental conditions. However, farm boundaries, plot information, crop cycles, and agricultural activity records are often managed separately. This makes it difficult to maintain an organized overview of agricultural operations and use environmental information effectively. 2. OUR SOLUTION SpaceXplore Tchiowa is a digital agricultural management platform developed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data”. The platform provides a structured digital workspace where farmers can register their farms, define geographical boundaries, divide farms into smaller plots, manage crop cycles, and maintain agricultural activity records. 3. HOW IT WORKS The platform currently supports the following main functions: Farm registration and geographical boundary mapping. Creation and management of agricultural plots within registered farms. Automatic calculation of plot areas in hectares. Recording of crop types, varieties, planting dates, expected harvest dates, and crop status. Management of crop cycles and preservation of historical records. Agricultural activity records, including observations, planting, fertilization, treatments, and harvesting. Geographical validation helps ensure that plots remain within their registered farm boundaries and prevents overlapping plot areas. 4. NASA DATA INTEGRATION The platform integrates NASA POWER data to provide environmental and meteorological information that can be considered alongside farmer-provided agricultural records. This combination creates an opportunity to better understand the relationship between agricultural activities and environmental conditions, supporting more informed farm planning and monitoring. 5. TECHNOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENT The project was developed as a web-based application using modern web technologies, Supabase and PostgreSQL for data management, PostGIS for geospatial operations, and Vercel for deployment and hosting. The development approach prioritizes data organization, geographical accuracy, modular architecture, and secure access to agricultural information. 6. CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION The main innovative aspect is the integration of geographical farm management, plot-level crop-cycle tracking, agricultural activity histories, and NASA environmental data within a single platform. Rather than treating satellite and environmental information as isolated data, SpaceXplore Tchiowa aims to make it more useful by connecting it with the actual farms and agricultural activities recorded by users. 7. INTENDED IMPACT AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT The project aims to support small-scale farmers and agricultural communities, particularly in regions where access to structured digital agricultural management tools is limited. Its intended impact includes better farm organization, improved agricultural traceability, easier monitoring of crop activities, and greater awareness of environmental conditions. SpaceXplore Tchiowa is currently a functional prototype. Future development will focus on expanding environmental data integration, conducting practical tests with farmers, and developing carefully validated agricultural decision-support capabilities.
